inspection_summary: Verified the frozen SHA-256 and Python str.splitlines() count of 1,918, then inspected every logical line. The source traces pRH from the arithmetic of polynomial/function fields through Artin's zeta polynomials, Schmidt's coordinate-free function-field framework, Gauss/CM point counting, Hasse's two elliptic-curve proofs, Deuring's correspondence and lifting ideas, later finite-field classification results, and a final historical analysis of where RH is mathematically situated. Formula extraction is often degraded but the principal mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose; two rational-point theorem displays lose a decisive negation and are isolated as extraction-defective.

accepted_units.title: Historical rooting through pRH avatars
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the unresolved classical RH from its finite-field avatar and frames analogous statements and proof methods as evidence about mathematical placement.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the complete introduction so the historical question and the Artin–Schmidt–Hasse sequence remain linked.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; names and chronology are directly recoverable from the text.

accepted_units.title: From autonomous polynomial arithmetic to an analytic zeta component
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how polynomial arithmetic modulo a prime was made structurally parallel to integer arithmetic, while algebraic number theory retained a distinct analytic zeta-function layer.
accepted_units.context_note: The Dedekind transition at lines 185–199 is needed to avoid reducing the unit to a disciplinary anecdote.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed Dedekind Euler product is degraded, but the prose identifies ideals and prime ideals.

accepted_units.title: Artin's quadratic function-field zeta polynomial and pRH
accepted_units.why_material: Transfers quadratic number-field organization to quadratic function fields, compresses the zeta problem into a finite polynomial, removes trivial zeros, and expresses pRH as a common modulus condition on its roots.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes arithmetic setup, Euler/Dirichlet decomposition, polynomial reduction, and the explicit distinction between Artin's roots and the modern normalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy with damaged product/sum glyphs; the polynomial reduction and modulus criterion are explicit enough for semantic use, but exact formulas need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: One Euler-product definition across rings and its RH questions
accepted_units.why_material: Presents maximal-ideal Euler products as a common representation for classical, Dedekind, polynomial-ring, and curve cases, then separates continuation, functional equation, and zero-location questions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes examples because they establish the transfer rather than merely illustrating notation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several product symbols are degraded; the prose and displayed denominators preserve the construction.

accepted_units.title: Extension-field point counts as a zeta generating series
accepted_units.why_material: Encodes the entire sequence of point counts over finite extensions into one formal power series, exposing zeta data as compressed dynamical information about Frobenius iterates.
accepted_units.context_note: The historical caveat at lines 402–406 distinguishes the modern encoding from what was explicitly available before 1940.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exponential/logarithmic displays have extraction noise but the point-count sequence and encoding role are legible.

accepted_units.title: Curve-zeta rationality, Frobenius factors, and pRH
accepted_units.why_material: Connects the Euler product of a smooth complete curve to a rational generating function whose numerator factors into Frobenius terms, making pRH a modulus constraint and point counts over extensions a power-sum readout.
accepted_units.context_note: The span retains Schmidt's rationality statement and the elliptic specialization needed to see the representation change.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula layer is imperfect, especially indices and conjugation bars; conceptual relations are stated in checked prose and displays.

accepted_units.title: Affine versus complete zeta functions and trace determination
accepted_units.why_material: Makes the places-at-infinity convention explicit and shows that, for a complete elliptic curve, one point count fixes the Frobenius trace and hence its quadratic zeta numerator.
accepted_units.context_note: Starts at the explicit convention warning; earlier numerical example is unnecessary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Short formulas are legible, though the word 'zeros' follows the source's convention for Frobenius factors.

accepted_units.title: Schmidt's coordinate-free arithmetic of function fields
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing Artin's chosen variable by all places of the function field incorporates infinity uniformly and lets Riemann–Roch support the functional equation in arbitrary genus.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the contrast with Artin's special class-number results to preserve what the generalization gains and leaves behind.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-supported; the single Euler factor is readable despite typography.

accepted_units.title: Functional equation, rationality, and pRH as three separate targets
accepted_units.why_material: Factorizes the early curve-zeta program into three logically distinct properties and records that Schmidt established the first two while Hasse handled pRH only for elliptic curves.
accepted_units.context_note: The polynomial presentation is included because it supplies the shared object to which all three properties apply.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The factorization display is usable with minor index/OCR noise.

accepted_units.title: Gauss's Last Entry as a bridge from congruences to elliptic point counts
accepted_units.why_material: Records an early empirical rule connecting biquadratic residues and lemniscatic functions through a congruence whose solution count later becomes an elliptic-curve count.
accepted_units.context_note: The original statement and the authors' identification of Fagnano's relation are both needed; the diary logistics are retained only as local provenance.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Original Latin/English and equation extraction are readable at the semantic level; exact congruence typography should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Normalize Gauss's curve and read its count as Frobenius norm
accepted_units.why_material: Turns Gauss's singular plane model into an elliptic normalization and identifies the counted quantity with the norm of Frobenius minus identity, yielding its characteristic polynomial.
accepted_units.context_note: The geometric normalization, four points above infinity, count, and Frobenius identification form one inseparable mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The plane equation appears to repeat a term and is formula-risky; the prose-supported normalization/norm mechanism is usable, exact model requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Point counting, Frobenius norm, and CM reduction
accepted_units.why_material: States pRH as a norm/point-count equivalence and explains characteristic-p point counting by reducing a controlled CM curve and its division points from characteristic zero.
accepted_units.context_note: The modern reformulation and the reduction argument are joined because together they expose the proof route rather than only the result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Some conjugation and square-root glyphs are damaged; prose identifies splitting, CM, reduction, and division-point injection.

accepted_units.title: Hasse's first proof via a chosen CM lift
accepted_units.why_material: Explains the strategic move of realizing a finite-field elliptic curve as the reduction of a suitably chosen CM curve so explicit class-field theory can control its points.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the motivation and the limitations concerning special automorphisms and historical lineage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant and stable.

accepted_units.title: CM lattice setup, ray-class reduction, and the odd-degree obstruction
accepted_units.why_material: Details how a lattice, factorization of a field power, congruent invariants, and division-point coordinates reduce counting to class-field theory, then isolates the j-invariant restriction as technical rather than intrinsic.
accepted_units.context_note: The full setup is needed to show what the lift must preserve and exactly where Hasse's method stalled.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent at lines 688–706 with degraded symbols; use as conceptual construction and verify exact equations before reuse.

accepted_units.title: The Hasse point-count bound as elliptic pRH
accepted_units.why_material: Makes the elliptic pRH operational as a square-root error bound for rational-point counts and records its extension from Artin's examples to all elliptic curves.
accepted_units.context_note: Standalone criterion following the first-proof discussion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Inequality is legible; strict versus non-strict convention is explicitly discussed in prose.

accepted_units.title: Elliptic curve versus genus-one curve without a rational point
accepted_units.why_material: Separates genus one from elliptic-curve structure by the rational-point/group-law requirement and notes why the distinction collapses over finite fields but not over arbitrary fields.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the equivalent viewpoints and the finite-field versus rational-field contrast.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Critical negation glyphs are dropped at lines 742 and 750; lines 745–753 make the intended distinction recoverable, but exact definitions require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Ordinary and supersingular elliptic curves through endomorphisms
accepted_units.why_material: Gives equivalent group-theoretic, endomorphism-ring, splitting, and abelian-variety characterizations of ordinary versus supersingular behavior, including the quaternionic endomorphism algebra.
accepted_units.context_note: The preliminary finite-field definability statements and terminology explain how the classification is interpreted.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several 'not equal/contains' glyphs render as control characters; equivalences are prose-supported but exact relation signs need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Supersingular parameters from a Hasse polynomial and symmetry orbits
accepted_units.why_material: Combines a polynomial criterion in Legendre form with an S3 action to count isomorphism classes as orbits, illustrating how parameter-space symmetry converts roots into moduli information.
accepted_units.context_note: The class-number formulas are context; the reusable mechanism is polynomial locus plus group quotient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy and OCR-risky; the orbit argument is clear in prose, while coefficients and exact substitutions need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: CM, finite-field definability, descent, and isogeny
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes being definable over a smaller field from descending a given model, and shows how base extension changes isomorphism classes even at fixed j-invariant; it also tracks the elliptic insight into higher-dimensional CM results.
accepted_units.context_note: The counterexamples at lines 898–912 are needed to prevent conflating field of moduli, definition, and descent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Some inclusion symbols are degraded; the prose distinctions are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Frobenius cases expose a base-field conflation in Hasse's criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Classifies ordinary and two supersingular Frobenius regimes, then diagnoses a historical false equivalence caused by mixing an algebraically closed curve with a Frobenius attached to a fixed finite field.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the historical claim and the authors' diagnosis so the classification functions as a falsifier rather than a catalogue.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conjugation bars, inequalities, and a stray question-mark glyph are unreliable; prose identifies the three cases and the ground-field error.

accepted_units.title: From Deuring's elliptic endomorphisms to Tate's homomorphism theorem
accepted_units.why_material: Shows a reusable generalization pattern: an elliptic-curve isomorphism between geometric homomorphisms and Galois-equivariant Tate-module maps motivates the corresponding theorem and conjectures for abelian varieties.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 969–971 are excluded as a separate historical uncertainty; this unit begins with the precise later transfer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The map's script-l symbols are degraded, but domain, codomain, and transfer claim are readable.

accepted_units.title: Supersingular curves away from Hasse's claimed boundary cases
accepted_units.why_material: Uses explicit Frobenius polynomials to falsify the claim that supersingularity occurs only at boundary trace values, and includes a nearby polynomial satisfying a naive bound but not realizable as elliptic Frobenius.
accepted_units.context_note: Both positive counterexamples and the non-realizability warning delimit the failed criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Arithmetic examples are legible enough to establish the logical role, but square-root/conjugation typography needs checking for exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Honda–Tate existence test for elliptic Frobenius polynomials
accepted_units.why_material: Partitions trace valuations and field degrees into ordinary existence, several supersingular existence regimes, and a forbidden regime, turning a magnitude bound into a realizability criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The conclusion and proof-route comments are retained to separate classification from explicit curve construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense formulas are extraction-risky and line 1044 appears internally inconsistent with the earlier bound; use the prose case split and verify exact inequalities against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Hasse's second proof from Frobenius norm and positive involution
accepted_units.why_material: Recasts elliptic pRH as the identity between Frobenius and its adjoint under the endomorphism-algebra involution, avoiding the chosen CM-lift restrictions of the first proof.
accepted_units.context_note: The isogeny/function-field correspondence closes the representation link.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The anti-involution arrow glyph is degraded; norm identity and conceptual role are clear.

accepted_units.title: A structural function-field framework as a research commitment
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why Hasse preferred his second proof: it embedded pRH in an intrinsic arithmetic theory of function fields and thereby shaped which higher-genus routes appeared natural.
accepted_units.context_note: The framing before subsection 9.1 is retained because it makes method preference causal rather than biographical.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; quoted German is translated in the source.

accepted_units.title: Competing higher-genus routes: abelian uniformization or algebraic methods
accepted_units.why_material: Transfers a principle from Siegel's function/value relations to congruence counting, forecasts higher-genus abelian uniformization, and explicitly keeps Weil's algebraic route as an alternative.
accepted_units.context_note: The later optimistic announcement of Deuring's idea shows what evidence seemed to resolve the choice.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Quoted prose is stable; no exact formulas.

accepted_units.title: Replace elliptic endomorphisms by self-correspondences
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies Deuring's key higher-genus abstraction: the endomorphism ring of an elliptic curve should become the ring of correspondences of a curve with itself, within Hasse's arithmetic function-field program.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the contemporaneous claim of algebraicity and the stated expectation that this foundation would support pRH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose and correspondence quotations are directly recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Analytic, geometric, and arithmetic languages for correspondences
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that the same object had analytic, Italian-geometric, and function-field presentations, with algebraization over arbitrary characteristic as the contested bridge.
accepted_units.context_note: The historical preconditions are part of the semantic comparison, not merely chronology.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant.

accepted_units.title: Algebraize correspondences, then supply differentials, norm, and positivity
accepted_units.why_material: Gives a concrete higher-genus program: form a ring of correspondences, develop its action on differentials, generalize norm by extension degree, and reduce pRH to positivity; it also records that the norm step was never supplied.
accepted_units.context_note: The quoted construction is retained through the authors' retrospective failure diagnosis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Field-compositum notation and mapping glyphs are imperfect; the missing-step structure and positivity target are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Weil's quotient ring and warning against discarding prior gauges
accepted_units.why_material: Recognizes Deuring's ring as correspondences modulo the ideal of valence zero and argues that translation into modern algebra should preserve older theories as diagnostic gauges.
accepted_units.context_note: The algebraic quotient and methodological warning jointly explain why representational equivalence mattered to the proof program.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose and quotient construction are legible.

accepted_units.title: Dialect fragmentation blocks a collective proof program
accepted_units.why_material: Documents how mathematically related approaches failed to coordinate because their practitioners used incompatible algebraic-geometric languages, while also separating that bottleneck from later proof priority disputes.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the workshop outcome and immediate consequences, not the surrounding correspondence already represented.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Historical prose; no formula dependency.

accepted_units.title: Intrinsic characteristic-p proof versus lifting and a later language shift
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts Hasse's allegiance to an intrinsic function-field proof with lifting to characteristic zero, then notes that eventual success required a newly consolidated algebraic-geometric language.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes both Hasse's stated preference and the retrospective qualification by Roquette's later proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant.

accepted_units.title: Lift an elliptic curve together with an endomorphism
accepted_units.why_material: States the exact repair to Hasse's first proof: every finite-field elliptic curve and chosen endomorphism admit a compatible characteristic-zero lift.
accepted_units.context_note: The definition of lifting is included so the theorem records preserved structure, not just existence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Tensor/isomorphism notation is slightly broken across lines 1415–1416; the lifting data are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Higher-dimensional lifting failures and isogeny-level CM repair
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that pair lifting generalizes to ordinary/almost-ordinary cases but fails for many higher-dimensional pairs, while CM lifting can be restored after a suitable isogeny and sometimes base extension.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeping failure and repaired statement together prevents overgeneralizing the elliptic theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-supported; some base-field and isogeny symbols are degraded.

accepted_units.title: A proof would mathematically root RH
accepted_units.why_material: Argues that superficial classification as special-function theory is inadequate because RH has many equivalent formulations and avatars; the eventual proof mechanism would provide its first non-provisional mathematical placement.
accepted_units.context_note: The span is self-contained and ties the final reflection back to the introduction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The xi display is degraded but not needed for the meta-level claim.

accepted_units.title: Disciplinary labels do not determine RH's proof route
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts Weil, Riemann's title and possible Dirichlet/Eisenstein influences, the breakup of arithmetic algebraic analysis, Kronecker's assessment, and later classification shifts to show that disciplinary placement is historically unstable.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins where explicit competing placements enter and ends with the source's unresolved assessment of analytic number theory.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Quoted prose and historical classification are stable; intervening analytic expressions are not required.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From zeta zeros to Frobenius dynamics
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source supports a progression in which Artin's polynomial roots are recast as Frobenius factors, extension-field point counts become their power-sum readout, and elliptic pRH becomes a norm/adjoint statement.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a within-source historical-conceptual synthesis; the source does not supply a higher-genus proof from these observations.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Lifting as a proof route and as a bounded theorem
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Gauss's CM example and Hasse's first proof use reduction from characteristic zero; Deuring later removes the elliptic lifting obstruction, while higher-dimensional counterexamples force an isogeny-level or ordinarity-qualified repair.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The accepted spans compare mechanisms across periods but do not establish the cited lifting theorems independently.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Endomorphisms generalize to correspondences, but positivity machinery remains
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Hasse's elliptic endomorphism-ring proof motivates Deuring's replacement by a ring of self-correspondences in higher genus, where missing differential, norm, and positivity components become the explicit obstruction.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source reports the program and its failure; it does not prove that completing exactly these steps would suffice.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Base field is part of Frobenius semantics
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Definability, descent, base extension, endomorphism growth, and Frobenius realizability must be tracked together; conflating them produces false supersingularity criteria that explicit examples and Honda–Tate cases expose.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several exact inequalities and relation glyphs are extraction-risky, so the synthesis is semantic and requires scan checks before formalization.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Representation choice can be a mathematical and coordination bottleneck
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Coordinate-free function fields, Italian algebraic geometry, analytic correspondence theory, and later algebraic geometry encode overlapping structures, but language preferences controlled which tools, prior results, and collaborators were visible to the pRH program.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The historical account supports this causal interpretation locally; it does not show that language unification alone would have produced a proof.

within_source_saturation: Whole-source saturation reached after 36 accepted units: every mathematical section was inspected, and the remaining spans are front matter/references, abstract or transition context, repetitive numerical instantiations of represented mechanisms, two formula-critical rational-point statements with dropped negations, or number-field rational-point material outside the pRH line. Further splitting would predominantly duplicate accepted constructions, criteria, comparisons, and obstructions.
stop_reason: Stopped at the source-specific endpoint after line 1918: sections 1–11 have accepted coverage for every distinct recoverable pRH mechanism and historical-method comparison; Artin/Gauss numerical tables are repetitive, the section 8 nonemptiness displays are extraction-defective, and lines 1578–1918 are bibliography. No quota or cross-source evidence was used.
